## p198 A — Prices and freight for wheat delivered to Poti

**Sources on this page:** p198 A. [Concise case study](../naval/p198_shipping_query.md).

<a id="edition-cases-naval-p198-shipping-query-p198-a--prices-and-freight-for-wheat-delivered-to-poti"></a>



**Conditional recovery: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.** Source-defined group
repairs and the registered **Nov7–9 key** recover a shipping-price query from
the irregular transmission on printed p198. The 244-slot model fixes
**111/122 raw positions**; five observed-coordinate substitutions and seven
fills give **118/122**.

<a id="edition-cases-naval-p198-shipping-query-conditional-shared-digits"></a>

### Conditional shared digits

**Readable German — conditional shared digits, with the existing source edition retained:**

> Drahtet Kaufpreis, Schiffsfracht, Transporversicherung fuer Ende Sept. mit Dampfer ??PASIA und IBALIA Poti gelieferte 116?0K Pud Weizen.

The [shared-reference assignment](../../experiments/nov7_9_joint_digits/README.md) gives **116?0K** from the unchanged VF pair at original source 109/158, raising this edition from **118 to 119/122** fixed labels. The opposite assignment gives 115?0K. All four minimum source maps and both C/G glyph alternatives retain this consequence; no ship name, full quantity or unit value is selected.

In the primary frame, the original 12 jointly attainable quantity strings reduce to **six** under the selected square, with **216** complete arithmetic witnesses rather than 432 across both squares. These are compatibility alternatives, not historical quantities. The two unresolved ship-name positions and one quantity mask remain.


<a id="edition-cases-naval-p198-shipping-query-p198-a"></a>

### p198 A

**Readable German — conditional word edition; received spelling, names and quantity retained:**

> Drahtet Kaufpreis, Schiffsfracht, Transporversicherung fuer Ende Sept. mit Dampfer ??PASIA und IBALIA Poti gelieferte 11??0K Pud Weizen.

The query asks for the purchase price, ship freight and transport insurance
for wheat delivered to Poti at the end of September. `TRANSPOR` lacks the T
of ordinary German *Transport*; the readable text preserves that spelling.
The steamer labels and `11??0K` quantity are retained exactly. No vessel
identity or numerical tonnage is supplied.

This is section **A**. The original p198 challenge is section **D** and has
its own separate status.

<a id="edition-cases-naval-p198-shipping-query-source-defined-frame"></a>

### Source-defined frame

The source advertises `RICHI-244` but prints **247 glyph slots**. Its first
two groups have six glyphs (`XADTAF`, `AATAGV`), `XGAX` has four, and the
ending contains six coordinates. The annotation says **Very irregular spark**.
All eight noncoordinate letters and both dashes remain in the literal source.

The selected conditional model excludes source indices **4, 8, 245 and 246**,
then inserts one unknown coordinate before original source index **92**.
Thus it excludes three observed coordinates and one invalid T, adds one
unknown slot, and retains all other source slots in order. The frame has
244 slots and uses the unchanged registered Nov7–9 square and ranks.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 244-slot frame; every printed mask and inserted slot unassigned:**

```text
DRAHT?TKAUFPREISS?HIFFSFRAC0TTRA?SP?RVERSICH?RUNGFUEYENDESEPTX?GTDAMPFER??PASIAUNDIBALIAPOTIXIELIEFERTEX11??0KXPUDWEIZE?XX
```

**Edited output — same frame; five observed substitutions, six printed-mask fills and one inserted-slot fill:**

```text
DRAHTETKAUFPREISSCHIFFSFRACHTTRANSPORVERSICHERUNGFUERENDESEPTXMITDAMPFER??PASIAUNDIBALIAPOTIXGELIEFERTEX11??0KXPUDWEIZENXX
```

</details>

The word corrections repair `FRAC0T`, `FUEY`, `?GT` and `IELIEFERTE`.
The numeral label `0` is changed only within the explicitly repaired word;
the separate `0` in the quantity remains unchanged.

Two source glyphs at indices 49 and 192 are C-like rather than clearly barred
G. The primary transcription preserves both as literal C and treats them as
masks. The ordinary word `WEIZEN` supplies one fill; the corresponding vessel
letter remains unknown. All four C/G combinations are checked separately.
Reading source 192 as G would give `?TPASIA`, but that alternative is not
silently selected in the primary edition.

<a id="edition-cases-naval-p198-shipping-query-four-tied-source-maps"></a>

### Four tied source maps

Every choice of one exclusion in each initial six-glyph group, one insertion
boundary in `XGAX`, and two exclusions in the final six coordinates is
checked: **2,700 maps**. The word template has four minima at five observed
substitutions. All exclude source 4 and the final 245–246, insert before 92,
and exclude one source position from `{6, 7, 8, 9}`.

All four give the same displayed raw and edited labels. The selected map
excludes only three observed coordinates; the others exclude four. Their
uncertainty differs: the initial `?` of `??PASIA` lies in `MPRUWY` for the
selected map, but one tied map permits any square label. These alternatives
are retained rather than choosing a vessel name. The enumeration prices this
declared template and does not prove a unique historical error mechanism.

The two quantity positions are also linked. One is an unassigned VF square
cell with labels `{5, 6}`; the other depends on a surviving printed mask and
the same globally injective square. There are **12 joint quantity strings**,
not 14 independent marginal combinations. With the selected first-two-label
name domains they produce **432 complete roundtrip witnesses**, all retained in the
certificate. None is selected as the historical quantity.

<a id="edition-cases-context-transport-197-198-most-likely-readings"></a>

### Most likely readings

<a id="edition-cases-context-transport-197-198-equipment-for-darmstadt--p197-c--p198-b"></a>

#### Equipment for Darmstadt — p197 C / p198 B

**Readable German:**

> Nachr.-Chef. [EINHAFEN: unclear designation]. Zwei US-Geraete nach Darmstadt
> verladen. Station bleibt bis [16X0???] betr.-bereit. Seifert.

**Meaning:** Chief of signals; an unidentified designation follows. Load two
`US` apparatuses for Darmstadt. Keep the station operational until an unresolved
date/time. Signed Seifert. The abbreviations are read as *Nachrichtenchef* and
*betriebsbereit*; their full spellings were not transmitted.

The source-supported editorial template is:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
NACHRCHEFXEINHAFENXZWEIUSGERAETENACHDARMSTADTVERLADENX
STATIONBLEIBTBIS16X0???BETRBEREITXSEIFERT
```

</details>

Of its **92 specified characters out of 95**, 91 have a complete coordinate
pair in at least one aligned witness. The `E` in `VERLADEN` additionally needs
an erasure fill. Across both witnesses that choice also requires one known
coordinate change above the attainable minimum: **19 changes rather than 18**.
This is an edited composite of conflicting copies, not a clean full reading
already present in either copy.

**Terminology:** `US` plausibly refers to contemporary radio apparatus using
undamped waves. The manufacturer's *Telefunken-Zeitung*, no. 15 (May 1919),
shows an apparatus labelled `Tragbares U S Gerät 17` on printed page 15 and
records delivery of a `U-S-Gerät` on page 16, beside its discussion of
undamped-wave equipment. This supports the equipment interpretation; it does
not identify the specific model in the telegram. See the
[primary journal](https://www.radiomuseum.org/forumdata/users/5100/TZ_3Jg_Nr15_1v1_v10.pdf#page=16)
and [terminology review](../../data/reviews/transport_terminology.json).

`EINHAFEN` is retained without a place identification. The date/time is not
silently normalized to 16:00: the witnesses actually disagree in its final
positions.

<a id="edition-cases-context-transport-197-198-lorry-trailer-and-petrol-pump--p197-d--p198-e"></a>

> Es kommt ein [?]-Tonnen-Auto. Nur besten [Anhaenger] beladen.
> [Benzinpumpe] bereithalten.

**Meaning:** A lorry of unresolved tonnage is coming. Load only the best
trailer and have the petrol pump ready. The bracketed words include explicit
editorial changes; the tonnage is not a recovered digit.

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
ESKOMMTEIN?TONNENAUTOXNURBESTENANHAENGERBELADENX
BENZINPUMPEBEREITHALTEN
```

</details>

Of **70 specified characters out of 71**, 66 have a complete observed pair,
one combines coordinate halves from the two witnesses, and three require
unattested coordinate changes. The preferred wording costs **13** known
coordinate changes across the two copies; their attainable minimum is **8**.
The extra changes affect `A`, `E` in `ANHAENGER` and `Z` in `BENZIN`.

<a id="edition-cases-context-transport-197-198-linked-number-fields"></a>

### Linked number fields

The shared partial square links several unresolved characters across the
conversation. These identities help future recovery without choosing a digit:

| Field | Shared square cell |
|---|---|
| Lorry tonnage in p197 D / p198 E | `FV` |
| Hour digit in the planned `1?00` departure, p194 A / p196 B | `FV` |
| Hour digit in the reported `1?00` departure, p197 E / p198 C | `AF` |
| Hour digit in the apparent readiness time `0?05`, p197 C | `GA` |
| Men remaining, p197 E / p198 C | `GD` |

The planned and reported hour digits therefore **differ** under the common
bijective square. The tonnage equals the planned-hour digit. Under the
published partial key, treating all four distinct fields as ordinary
decimal digits gives **360** assignments. A same-day departure no later
than the `13.45` origin field could then be 12:00 or 13:00. Further assuming
the same movement and prohibiting early departure gave the earlier scenario
“planned 12:00, departed 13:00, a 2-ton lorry.”

The [shared conditional VG=2 interpretation](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/README.md#the-award-class)
changes that comparison. Digit 2 belongs to VG and cannot also occupy
either hour cell. The four decimal fields now have **120** assignments.
If the reported departure is same-day and before `13.45`, it must be
**13:00**, assigning **AF=3**; **24** joint field assignments remain. The
planned-hour/tonnage cell FV is then one of `4, 7, 8, 9`.

No assignment satisfies the additional “no early departure” condition.
The earlier 12:00/13:00 scenario and the new award-class interpretation are
therefore incompatible within this square. Neither the common-movement
assumption nor the chronology is supplied by the ciphertext. The current
readings retain the unknown time fields, with the 13:00 branch recorded
separately in the [joint transport certificate](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/transport_certificate.json).
The p198 C source itself prints a `13.03 p.m.` receipt before its `13.45`
origin time, so the recorded times cannot all be accepted without qualification.

The [linked-field analysis](../../experiments/transport_followup/linked_fields.json)
records the exact source indices and the earlier three scenario counts; its separate
enumeration checks every one of the square's 40,320 bijective completions.
An [independent review](../../data/reviews/transport_linked_fields_independent.json)
reconstructs the mappings by column offsets and confirms that every tied
source geometry gives the same field identities.

<a id="edition-cases-context-transport-197-198-what-was-repaired"></a>

### What was repaired

| Source | Literal evidence | Stated reconstruction |
|---|---|---|
| p197 C | 185 slots against a `RIZI-190` label; six dashes and an invalid `C` | Insert five unknown coordinates. All 186 boundaries were checked; positions 64 and 65 tie and yield the same masked stream. |
| p198 B | 190 valid coordinates | Kept as printed; its disagreements with the proposed reading are recorded separately. |
| p197 D | 142 slots, including one dash at position 89 | A conditional relocation of that dash preserves the order of every known coordinate. Positions 74 and 75 tie among all 142 placements; both survive. |
| p198 E | 147 slots against a `RIZI-142` label; adjacent `XAXVV XAXVV` and an invalid `K` | Delete either identical five-coordinate group. Both deletions give the same 142-slot stream, preserving 141 valid coordinates. |

All positions above are zero-based. Minimum disagreement is an alignment
criterion; it does not establish that a proposed loss or misplaced dash
actually occurred. The two raw source readings, every tied geometry, and all
per-letter alternatives are available in the
[full experiment](../../experiments/transport_followup/README.md).

<a id="edition-cases-context-transport-two-vehicles-and-two-trailers--p189-e"></a>

#### Two vehicles and two trailers — p189 E

**Readable German — conditional shared VG=2, with one invalid-coordinate fill:**

> Ja, Hebepumpe aus Blech. Kommen 2 Autos. Hier 2 Anhaenger.

The [award-class interpretation](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/README.md#the-award-class)
supplies **VG=2** to both count fields, at plaintext positions **26 and 37**.
The word `ANH?ENGER` has the partial pair `V?`, with the invalid printed `B`
at source position **81**. Filling it as **V** gives `ANHAENGER`. This takes
the native 94-slot message from **44 to 47/47** fixed positions: two digits
from the shared square and one ordinary-word fill, with **no observed-coordinate
substitution**. The source's `B` remains visible in the literal transcription.
Indices are zero-based. [Exact completion and source mapping](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/transport_certificate.json).

<a id="edition-cases-context-transport-p185-d-source-and-gap-model"></a>

### p185 D source and gap model

![Literal p185 D source excerpt](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p185_D.png)

We enumerated all 194 possible positions for a contiguous block of five missing coordinates under the audited November 13–15b key. Every valid received coordinate remains unchanged and in its original order. No missing coordinate or unknown square cell is filled.

<a id="edition-cases-context-transport-conditional-result"></a>

### Conditional result

Inserting five erasures before source index **55**, a printed group boundary, gives this exact partial plaintext:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional five-coordinate gap before source index 55:**

```text
STATMETXMARSCHIERTLCST?UT?SMORGEN1500UEBERDHFNXAB?A6SCHBE?EITSEIN?VS6GROV?AN?IERE?XBITTEF6EXSEIFERT
```

</details>

Under this geometry, **91 of 99 characters are fixed**. The eight unresolved positions consist of six positions touched by uncertain coordinates and two positions using unassigned square cells. The fixed portions include `MARSCHIERT`, `MORGEN1500UEBERDHFN`, and `SEIFERT`; malformed portions are retained literally. `DHFN` and `STATMET` are not expanded into place or station names.

This is a conditional result. The strongest composite language score selects position 55, but a conventional plaintext quadgram score selects position 57:

| Gap before source index | Composite ranking score | Plaintext quadgram mean |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 55 | 24.910328 | -6.041730 |
| 56 | 22.691041 | -6.070230 |
| 57 | 22.641029 | -5.987314 |

These are heuristic scores, not confidence probabilities. All 194 positions are arithmetically compatible with the received symbols. Positions 159 and 160 produce the same masked ciphertext because the inserted gap can exchange places with the existing unknown `Y` slot. There are 193 distinct masked ciphertexts. No plaintext character is fixed across all 194 geometries. The three leading composite-score candidates share 89 fixed characters, but that selected subset is not a confidence set.

### Independent transport context

Six additional source-checked intercepts decrypt directly with the same historical key. They retain every literal garble and unresolved square cell:

- **p193 E, November 14:** `KLEINERFEDERWAGENZU?ANHAENGENHIERXKOMMTAUTOX`
- **p194 A, November 14, header `CM v CZ`:** `ABTRANSPORTINVERABREDETERWEISEFREITCGDHFN1?00XWAGENBERE?THALTENXMARSCHZIELHANAUXSEIFERT`
- **p196 B, November 15, header `CM v CZ`:** `ABTRANSPORTINVERABREDETERWEISEFREITAGDHFN1?00XWAGENBEREITHALTENXMARSCHZIELHANAUXSEI?ERT`
- **p197 E, November 15, header `CM v CZ`:** `LASTAUTO1?00A?GEFAHRENXICHBLEIBEMIT?MANNBISSOHNTAGXALLESGUTEAUFWIEDERSEHENXSE?FERTXGRUSSBOCHO`
- **p198 C, November 15, header `CM v CZ`:** `LASTAUTO1?00ABGEFAHRENXICHBLEIBEMIT?MANNBISSONNTAGXALLESGUTEAUFWIEDERSEHENXSEHFERTXGRUSSBOCHO`
- **p189 E, November 15, header `CZ v CM`:** `JAHEBEPUMPEAUSBLECHXKOMMEN?AUTOSXHIER?ANH?ENGER`. This is a different intercept from the p189 challenge target.

The p194/p196 pair repeats `DHFN` and names `HANAU` as the march destination. It has 171 of 174 raw coordinates in common; disagreements are at indices 82 (`K/X`), 167 (`X/V`), and 173 (`D/G`). The p197/p198 pair agrees at 183 of 186 coordinates, differing at indices 59 (`V/A`), 63 (`A/V`), and 67 (`G/A`). Neither lorry-message copy supplies an exact `SEIFERT` signature; `SEHFERT` is not silently corrected.

between disagreeing source witnesses, with every chosen value attested in
at least one. The certificate retains all four combinations of the two
disagreements between valid coordinates. The planned-time cell `FV`
remains unassigned.

Under the separate shared VG=2 interpretation, the reported-hour cell
`AF` cannot also be 2. If the departure occurred on the report's date
before its `13.45` origin time, `1?00` therefore becomes **13:00**. That
chronological assumption is kept separate from the source-supported
composite. The [linked-field comparison](#edition-cases-context-transport-197-198-linked-number-fields)
also shows why this reading cannot be combined with the earlier extra
assumption that the reported departure was no earlier than the planned one.

The [certificate](../../data/certificates/p185_D_transport.json) contains every gap geometry, its full plaintext domains, exact source-to-plaintext mapping, all six direct context readings, both near-parallel comparisons, and the conditional composite. The [standalone verifier](../../adfgvx/transport.py) recomputes all 194 constraint sets and exact coordinate roundtrips without a language model. It checks the consistency of the stored ranking order but does not recompute the heuristic scores. The [portable ranking script](../../experiments/known_key/README.md) reproduces both complete rankings from a pinned upstream model; every stored score matched exactly in the recorded environment.

```sh
python3 -m adfgvx.transport
```

This analysis does not fully solve p189 and does not add a solved item to the 22-message total.

Four [additional p197/p198 witnesses](#edition-cases-context-transport-197-198) now connect the
conversation with equipment for Darmstadt, a lorry, a trailer and a petrol
pump. Their duplicate-group and missing-coordinate hypotheses have separate
source and arithmetic certificates.

Source images: [p189](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p189_context.png), [p193](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p193_context.png), [p194](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p194_context.png), [p196](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p196_context.png), [p197](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p197_context.png), [p198](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p198_context.png). Header order is `recipient v sender`; see [source conventions](../../sources/README.md).

## p198 — Open CHI intercept with a length shortfall

**Sources on this page:** p198. [Concise case study](../p198.md).

<a id="edition-cases-p198-p198--open-chi-intercept-with-a-length-shortfall"></a>



**Status:** No accepted plaintext. **Current source and attack review:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. Original challenge: [Lasry–Schmeh](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/unsolved-adfxvx-messages-from-world-war-i/).

<a id="edition-cases-p198-most-likely-reading"></a>

### Most likely reading

No defensible plaintext has yet been identified. The source and the best tested hypotheses are recorded below; no language-ranked diagnostic is promoted to a historical reading.

| Source fact | Value |
|---|---|
| Printed page / PDF page | 198 / 201 |
| Section | D |
| Received slots | 165 |
| Valid coordinates / uncertain slots | 165 / 0 |
| Header | `PZU v CM (18.27 p.m., November 15th); 18.45; CHI-170` |

VXVFV GFVFG DGVFG FFFGV VVGGG XVFXF XXFVD VDFDD FXAAX VVXAA

The [catalog](../../data/messages.json) retains the literal source, conservative analysis layer, and earlier online transcription separately. Headers follow `recipient v sender`.

<a id="edition-cases-p198-length-qualification"></a>

### Length qualification

The header advertises **CHI-170**, while the body contains **165 valid coordinates**. No erased group is explicitly printed. A single five-coordinate loss is a plausible model, but the source does not establish its location or contiguity. Ordinary complete ADFGVX requires an even coordinate count; silent truncation is not accepted.

This challenge target is **section D**. The separately readable
[p198 C transport message](#edition-cases-context-transport) and the newly linked
[p198 B/E equipment and lorry orders](#edition-cases-context-transport-197-198) use the
`RIZI` identifier and do not solve this `CHI` entry. Section E contains one
extra five-coordinate group, but moving that group into D is only a tested
corruption hypothesis, not an established source repair.

<a id="edition-cases-p198-attack-status"></a>

### Attack status

No accepted plaintext. Bounded missing-group and component-reuse searches preserve the 165 valid coordinates under their declared length hypotheses. [The experiment index](../../experiments/README.md) records completed scopes and controls. Unknown keys, noncontiguous losses, other corruption models, and header errors remain unexcluded.

<a id="edition-cases-p198-exact-scattered-loss-experiments"></a>

#### Exact scattered-loss experiments

The [marginal decoder](../../experiments/p198_exact_sparse/README.md) covers all
**1,115,034,284** possible positions of five scattered losses for each supplied
complete key. The [joint decoder](../../experiments/p198_joint_exact/README.md)
also chooses their six-valued coordinates consistently, covering
**8,670,506,592,384 loss-and-fill witnesses**. The latter count includes aliases;
it does not count distinct plaintexts.

The recorded historical runs fix one transposition and one heuristic
completion of each of two partial squares. Neither gives a readable result.
The joint four-gram objective also selects wrong plaintexts in both synthetic
controls even when supplied with the true complete keys. The source witnesses,
exact scores and failures are retained. These experiments resolve the search
optimum under their stated assumptions; they do not establish a historical key,
validate the damage model, or solve p198.

The [six-gram calibration](../../experiments/p198_joint_six/README.md) does recover
one complete 85-position control, including its exact loss mask and fills, under
both pure-six and mixed objectives. A feasible wrong competitor still beats
the other control's truth under both objectives. This improves the demonstrated
capability of the method while preserving its remaining scoring limitation.

The subsequent [historical pure-six run](../../experiments/p198_six_historical/README.md)
under the frozen CHI13 completion changes the best geometry and improves its
six-gram objective, but the full result remains unreadable. At that selected
geometry, the conservative partial square has 48 singleton positions; this is
a conditional diagnostic, not 48 newly recovered plaintext positions. The report keeps
the entire model output and its disagreements with four-gram ranking.

<a id="edition-cases-p198-exact-constraints-without-a-language-model"></a>

#### Exact constraints without a language model

An independent [letter-count bound](../../experiments/p198_letter_bounds/README.md)
covers **all 40,320 completions** of the partial Nov13–15b square, with its
recorded transposition and every five-loss placement/fill. The attainable
ordinary-letter counts range from 44 to 82, so this family requires at least
three digits among the 85 plaintext positions. This is a modest exact
constraint without a language model; the actual message's digit count is
unknown, so it does not reject the key.

A stronger [category audit](../../experiments/p198_letter_bounds/CATEGORY_BOUNDS.md)
gives `digits + Q + Y ≥ 10` throughout the same partial-key family. If a proposed
plaintext contains no Q or Y, it must therefore contain at least ten digits;
a witness attains that bound. A separate Python algorithm factors the problem
into adjacent-column pairs and fully recomputes the optimum, independently of
the original C++ decoder. Neither inequality assumes that the historical text
had a particular digit or Q/Y count.

The complete [digit/Q/Y frontier](../../experiments/p198_category_frontier/README.md)
sharpens those separate inequalities. The following count pairs are attainable,
and every other attainable pair has at least as many digits and Q/Y positions
as one of these:

| Digit positions | Minimum Q/Y positions at that digit count |
|---:|---:|
| 3 | 13 |
| 4 | 6 |
| 5 | 5 |
| 6 | 4 |
| 7 | 3 |
| 8 | 2 |
| 9 | 1 |
| 10 | 0 |

Thus **three digits force at least thirteen Q/Y occurrences**, rather than
the seven allowed by the separate inequalities alone. Every frontier point
has a complete source-preserving witness. Two separate algorithms exhaust
all 28 letter/digit membership classes and their 15,504 loss allocations;
285,264 short exhaustive witnesses include an explicit control with two
incomparable count pairs. Different points may require different square
completions. These exact counts constrain future proposals within this
family; they do not supply a readable historical message or reject the key.

<a id="edition-cases-p198-conditional-restriction-from-an-independently-attested-name"></a>

#### Conditional restriction from an independently attested name

The [Tiflis appointment](../other/tiflis_appointment.md) supplies a separate
historical-name argument for **Nov13–15b FX = Y**. If that inference and the
Nov13b/five-loss hypothesis for p198 are both accepted, the exact family
shrinks to 5,040 complete squares. Its digit/QY frontier is
`(4,6), (5,5), (6,4), (7,3), (8,2), (10,1), (13,0)`.
Thus at least four digits are required, or at least thirteen if the reading
contains no Q or Y. The [conditional certificate](../../experiments/contextual_key_constraints/README.md)
preserves all received coordinates, supplies witnesses for every frontier
point, and independently recomputes all seven retained membership classes.
Neither the historical counts nor this key's applicability to p198 are
established. No plaintext position becomes fixed from this count result.

<a id="edition-cases-p198-why-individual-positions-remain-open"></a>

#### Why individual positions remain open

For either frozen complete-key hypothesis, **each of the 85 positions can
contain any of the 36 alphabet symbols in some compatible five-loss witness**.
The construction marks that position's two ciphertext coordinates as lost,
puts the remaining three losses elsewhere, and fills the selected pair with
the desired character. Every received coordinate still appears unchanged and
in order.

The [constructive domain audit](../../experiments/p198_letter_bounds/domain_witnesses.json)
checks all **6,120** key/position/symbol witnesses and exact re-encryption.
Each choice can use a different witness; arbitrary choices at all positions
need not coexist in one plaintext. That is why full individual domains can
coexist with the joint requirement of at least three digits. Additional source
evidence about the missing positions could narrow those domains.

```sh
python3 experiments/p198_letter_bounds/domain_witnesses.py --verify
```

The [direct source-similarity search](../../experiments/source_similarity/README.md)
also checks all 788 extracted OCR blocks. Its leading p198 candidate is p154 A2;
independent page inspection confirms only a short local resemblance and does
not establish a parallel transmission.
